questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a combination of different things. But mostly it was about experiencing a new culture and get a good challenge and experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Perfect city to live in. Kind people at UB. Only thing is that the educational level was a bit low compared to what I am used to. However, all in all great expereince

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Okay easy, but not completely easy. At UB in the autumn semester you can both take continous assessment and single-evaluation assessment. I did not know that and thereby thought that the exams where laying different than what they actually very.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Good. university of Copenhagen provided me with what I needed. Only critic of them is they answer very slow

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in an Airbnb apartment with 3 other danes.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is possible, but housing is not cheap in Barcelona. What is cheap is daily costs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really search a lot besides Airbnb.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that easy. i did not think the communication with UB was that smooth, but I had a different case than most people, so probably eassier for you

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Okay, but it was a bit messy. Again, my case was special because I was a first semester master student.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could call or text for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that successfully. But my case was not normal, so probably easier for you.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get going early in order to have everything going smooth.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of courses very in spanish, and the level of education was far from University of Copenhagen

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4th year BA courses which corresponded to 1th year master courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Low quality. More like High school set-up with class presentations and so on. Not bad, but way lower than at University of Copenhagen

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Managing Organizations. Global Sustainability. Business and Culture in Asia. Governance, institutions and public sector. Sustainable development.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Business and Culture in Asia and Governance, institutions and public sector is the only courses I would recommend of the ones I had. The teachers where good in these courses, and I think for most people it will all be new what is teached.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, coffee and generally going out for drinks, coffee or food is very cheap. Barcelona is an awesome city for you if you like to go to restaurants, café's and bars. Try La Flauta:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The options where there. However I mostly went to the gym instead. That was not a gym connected to the University

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of Erasmus activities. A trip to Marocco for example.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to cities in Catalonia. You can by a T-Mobilitat card and have free access to for example Sitges which is a nice city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy for me. I did not have difficulty adjusting to the spanish culture. the people are sweet and the environment very relaxed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to places where the locals are. For example if you like Clubs go to "Wolf".

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed atmosphere. Spanish people are kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get your documents done early (for example OLA). Go if you weight the social aspect high and the education less high. Get a T-Mobilitat card with 7 zones so that you can experience a lot in Catalonia

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really. Have fun, it is the perfect city for it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The atmosphere in the city and the people I lived with. we where close all 4 and had a lot of fun. I repeat myself but I think this is the essential question about whether you should go to Barcelona. "Do you like to go out"? If yes go to Barcelona. With go out I mean bars, clubs, restaurants and so on.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me it was actually getting used to talking english. Writing and reading a lot of english is one thing, but talking it every day is something else.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
